title: Twice through
author: Heather Bedle (example of a case submitted as a JSON file)
summary: Reflections step up to the east, and one well logs the same-looking sand twice.
brief: Reflections east of a moderately dipping surface sit higher than their counterparts to the west. W2 logs two sands of similar thickness and character where W1 logs one.

wells.name: W1
wells.note: Modern wireline suite: gamma ray, caliper, resistivity, density, neutron, sonic.

wells.name: W2
wells.note: Vertical well. Cuttings descriptions report the same fine sandstone at both levels.

W2.note: Footwall Sand B below the fault.

candidates.label: Reverse fault
candidates.description: A [[reverse-fault]] with the [[hanging-wall]] up to the east, formed under horizontal shortening.
pros: Reflections east of the fault are higher by a similar amount at every level.
A borehole crossing a reverse fault logs part of the section twice, as W2 does for Sand B.

candidates.label: Strike-slip fault
candidates.description: A [[strike-slip]] fault whose horizontal motion appears as reverse separation on this line.
pros: No strike information is available from one line.
cons: Repetition of a unit in a vertical well is not an expected result of strike-slip motion on a planar fault.

candidates.label: Two similar sands, no repetition
candidates.description: W2 penetrated two separate sand bodies with similar log character; the offset of reflections has another cause.
pros: Sands of similar thickness and log shape are common in a cyclic succession.
cons: W1 has only one sand at this level, 1.9 km away.
The two W2 sands bracket the depth where the discontinuity crosses the well.

evidence.label: Reflections higher east of the discontinuity
Two Sand B-like units in W2
The two sands bracket the fault crossing in W2
Cuttings descriptions identical at both levels

outcome.statement: The section was built with a reverse fault of 110 m throw that W2 crosses at about 910 m.
outcome.basis: Log character alone cannot prove two sands are the same unit. Biostratigraphy or a dipmeter across the fault would raise confidence further.

debrief: The fault crosses W2 between the two sands. The upper sand is Sand B in the hanging wall; the lower is Sand B again in the footwall.
